The STAR GeneCounts adopt keeps column 2 of `ReadsPerGene.out.tab` (unstranded) as the one gene table of every result, since no plan records the library's strandedness (`STARPlanRequest` in `STARPlanTypes.swift:71-85` has no strand field) and the chain counts unstranded (`STARPlan+Pipeline.swift:31-33,42-43`). A person with a stranded library therefore gets the unstranded count, a true count by a named rule, and no count by strand. BIO's ruling has the adopt name the column in the route's `geneCountsColumn` words, warn when the strand share is below 0.4 or above 0.6, and keep the whole file under `source/<sample>/` so columns 3 and 4 stay readable. Every library measured is unstranded (strand share 0.498 to 0.511 on 10 files), and on the seven real runs a wrong column would change about half of each gene's count on 17,000 to 22,000 genes a run, which would be S1, so no adopt picks column 3 or 4 until a setting exists. The fix is a plan setting `strandedness` (unstranded, forward, reverse) that the adopt maps to column 2, 3 or 4 and whose other values it refuses in words. EX-PLAN-STAR takes it (lge-lane-opus, BIO review).

The decoy maximum is a measured bound of about one in 1,000 for each barcode, not the stated 1e-6/12 (about 8e-8). Eight times the decoys (9,600) lower the worst file's rate about 6-fold (0.25% to 0.042%), still about 5,000 times the stated level, and raise the reads a lone real sample needs 8- to 14-fold, to about 1% of an amplicon file. A decoy floor's ceiling (4.5 to 32% of reads) would refuse a real 48-plex pool (about 2.1% of reads a sample), so a fix needs an anchored search that then takes the start-composition floor. That is a redesign for a later phase, after a BIO ruling on where Fluidigm barcodes sit. The words on every route name the case and the check (`DemultiplexEngine.swift:19-20`). Notes line for the next Preview, Things to know: "- **Exact Bare Barcode checks no chance.** On reads that do not carry the chosen barcodes, it makes a sample file for any barcode found by chance anywhere in a read, and in amplicon reads one such file can hold most of the reads. Use it only for reads that carry those barcodes, and check the sample files against your sample sheet."

effect: Three Cutadapt routes still write linked lines with no anchored side, so cutadapt searches each side anywhere in the read and counts 3 bases of a side at a read end. They are the sample-sheet route of a paired kit (`DemultiplexingPipeline.swift:1268-1308`), which writes `fwd...rc(rev)` and `rev...rc(fwd)` with the bare context (`PlatformAdapterContext.swift:299-305`) and ignores `--location`, and the long-read single and symmetric branches with `linkedSpec` (`:1326`, `:1386`). The sample-sheet route is reached only from sample assignments made in the App (`FASTQOperationDialogState.swift`, `FASTQDerivativeServiceModels.swift`), since the CLI has no sample-sheet option. The same unanchored form on the observed-pair route placed 8.1% to 11.3% of real reads with no barcode at error 0 and 74.0% to 82.2% at 0.15 (cutadapt 5.2). Since DEMUX-SATKIT (413bdd7a1) preflight refuses such lines at every error rate in words, so a person who demultiplexes with a sample sheet in the App sees the refusal, and with Keep Unchecked Samples gets sample files the chance floor did not check. No default run makes a chance sample. A fix anchors these lines as lane DEMUX-DUAL-ANCHOR anchored the observed-pair route (`^N{a}first...secondN{b}$`), or exempts a kit only when every line has two sides and every side keeps at least 12 exact bases at its shortest accepted match (`k - floor(e x k) >= 12`, with `k = min(side length, effectiveMinimumOverlap)` and `e = effectiveErrorRate`, BIO-DUAL-TESTS Q2). A `lge-ruling` BIO measure comes first.

Since lane DEMUX-DUAL-ANCHOR a custom dual-index file at Both Ends with no sample sheet is searched only at the read ends, and `--max-distance-5prime` and `--max-distance-3prime` (the dialog's 5' Distance and 3' Distance) are the offsets of both strands (`DemultiplexingPipeline.swift:1603-1608` at the lane head 1f0ba32d6). A read of the other strand of a molecule whose two flanks differ has them the other way round, so at 52/47 a molecule with 52 bases before i7 and 47 after i5 gives other-strand reads 47 before and 52 after, which fall outside and go to Unassigned (cutadapt 5.2). The tests build the other-strand read with the forward's flanks, so none catches it. ONT adapters sit at the read start of both strands and are not hit. The notes tell a person to use the longer distance for both. A `lge-ruling` BIO decides whether to mirror the other strand's offsets.

Only the observed-pair route of a custom dual kit caps its Cutadapt lines at 6,000 (lane DEMUX-DUAL-ANCHOR). `writeLinkedAdapterFASTA` for built-in dual kits and `writeSingleEndAdapterFASTA` (`DemultiplexingPipeline.swift:1449-1475` at the lane head 1f0ba32d6) write one line for each pair of offsets with no cap, and Cutadapt 5.2 spends about 29 ms a line at `-j 4` before its first read, so a large 5' Distance or 3' Distance makes a run sit for minutes or hours before any read with no words.

Two demultiplex refusals name no fix that works. `noBarcodeAboveChance` (`DemultiplexError.swift:67`) says to check the barcodes and the read end and names no distance, so a person whose barcodes sit in from the read ends reruns at distance 0 and gets the same words. The line cap of lane DEMUX-DUAL-ANCHOR (`:77`) tells a person with more than 3,000 pairs to lower distances that are already 0, where the fix is to split the barcode file, and it names no tool for trimming a known flank (Trim Fixed Bases, Adapter Removal).

Preview 2026.11.12 refuses a custom dual-index file at Both Ends with no sample sheet unless the person chooses Keep Unchecked Samples, and a run kept that way still searches each pair anywhere in the read, so its samples can hold chance reads (8 to 11 in 100 at error rate 0 and 74 to 82 in 100 at 0.15 on reads with no barcodes). A built-in Illumina dual kit (truseq-ht-dual, nextera-xt-v2, idt-ud-indexes) searched in the read bases, with the engine `cutadapt` or with no engine and fewer than 2 kit barcodes in the first read names (`DemultiplexSearchRoute.swift:47-52`, `:107-120`), looks at Both Ends for `i7...rc(i5)` (`DemultiplexingPipeline+Preflight.swift:49-51`) and, since lane DEMUX-DUAL-BARE-REVERSE, for its reverse strand `i5...rc(i7)`. A real Illumina construct reads `i5 ... i7` on its top strand and `rc(i7) ... rc(i5)` on its bottom strand, inside the P5 and P7 flanks, so the use the CLI help names, "internal Illumina barcodes within ONT reads" (`FastqCommand.swift:168-169`), places no real read with either form (cutadapt 5.2, 0 of 10 reads of each strand at error 0). A person who runs it gets every read in Unassigned and no read in a wrong sample. The layout is the ruling's reading of the Illumina oligos and not in the repository (medium-high confidence). A `lge-ruling` BIO rules the layout and the fix, a search form that matches the construct or help words that drop the use, before any lane.

A run of several inputs, or a Grouped Result of datasets that chose different secondary forms, shows one information line for each different form or count, and no line names its input or dataset. `secondaryFormLine(for:)` (`Sources/LungfishApp/Services/FASTQDemultiplexChanceNotice+Floor.swift:130-146`) reads the `secondaryForm` and `secondaryFormVotes` of each run folder's record and keeps each different line once, so the lines differ only by their counts or their form, and a person cannot tell which pool read which form. The floor's limit line names the input (`:66` of the same file). The fix is a line that names the input or dataset and a split of the row's information text (`informationParts`) that survives the name. The words are UX's and no result changes.

The refusal `dualFormUndecided` (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Demultiplex/DemultiplexError.swift:74-84`) ends with a step for one case only, a row that is not in the pool ("If one of these rows is not in this pool, remove it from the definition and run again."). A person whose pool holds both rows of the pair gets no step, and this version cannot tell the two rows apart (ruling BIO-DUAL-FORM Q4). The Known limit line for the notes has the same one-sided phrase (`~/lungfish-phase-records/demux-dual-bare-reverse-2026-11-18/rulings/UX-WORDS-2.md:221`). UX and BIO rule a closing sentence such as "If both are in this pool, this version cannot split them." for the refusal and the notes line together.

The sentence of `noBarcodeAboveChance` that says the way the secondary sequences are written is not the cause (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Demultiplex/DemultiplexError.swift:109-112`) is added whenever the run made a choice of form (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Demultiplex/DemultiplexingPipeline+DualForm.swift:191-193`), also when `rowsCarrying` is 0 because no row had more than 3 reads that only one form places. In a pool of a few reads for each row in a large file the form could be the cause, and the sentence says it is not. A `lge-ruling` BIO confirms or narrows the flag, for example to a choice with `rowsCarrying` above 0, and UX words the refusal for the case where the sentence stays out.

The vote of the choice of secondary form counts a barcode base as matching only when it equals the read's base or is N (`matches` in `Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Demultiplex/DemultiplexingPipeline+DualForm.swift:260-268`). A Custom Definition may hold every IUPAC letter (`Sources/LungfishIO/Formats/FASTQ/IlluminaBarcodeKits.swift:179`), and Cutadapt matches those letters as sets. A row with two or more such letters in a barcode of 8 to 10 bases casts no vote, so the run falls back to the secondary sequence as written, and the refusal that can follow says the way the column is written is not the cause. A fix lets the vote match IUPAC letters as Cutadapt does, with a test. It is rare.

When a run reads the secondary sequence reverse complemented, the barcode rows of `demux-manifest.json` keep the column as the file gives it (`barcodeSequenceInfo`, `Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Demultiplex/DemultiplexingPipeline.swift:1912`), and only the run's record names the form (`secondaryForm` and `secondaryFormVotes`, `Sources/LungfishCLI/Commands/FastqCommand.swift:495-497`). A reader of the manifest alone cannot tell which form the run searched. The lane kept the form out of the manifest, as it keeps the chance floor out of it, so that the manifest stays as it was (BIO review of DEMUX-DUAL-FORM, deviation 6, accepted). BIO rules whether the manifest names the form, with a test that reads it.

Preflight makes the choice of the secondary form before it refuses a kit whose barcodes are too short for the check for chance matches. `createAdapterConfiguration` writes the lines and makes the choice (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Demultiplex/DemultiplexingPipeline+Preflight.swift:91`, `DemultiplexingPipeline.swift:1449`), and `requireChanceCheckableKit` comes after it (`+Preflight.swift:93`). A Custom Definition of dual indexes with barcodes short enough that chance votes fall in many rows could get `dualFormMixed` where the kit is the cause and `chanceCheckCannotJudgeKit` would say so. It is rare. A fix asks for the check for chance matches first or orders the two refusals, with a test of a definition with short barcodes.

The sample correlation that `lungfish-cli rnaseq quality` prints (Pearson r of log2(CPM + 1) over the host genes with a count above 0 in a sample) depends on the gene filter, and so on the other samples of the result: C1 `A_1`-`A_2` reads 0.9918 there, 0.9881 on the genes seen in those two samples alone and 0.9934 on all genes (C5 `RICC_1001`-`RICC_1003` 0.9839, 0.9788, 0.9862). A person who reads a correlation plot without its caption, or who compares two results with different sample sets cell by cell, sees a difference that the filter makes. RS-BULK-VIEW-M2 must show the caption with the plot.

The rRNA share of `rnaseq quality` is the share of counts on annotated rRNA genes (biotype `rRNA` or `Mt_rRNA` in `genes.tsv`). GENCODE 32 lists 58 `rRNA` genes (5S and 5.8S), and reads of 28S and 18S fall on no gene, so the figure cannot say how well depletion worked. A view that calls it rRNA contamination or rRNA content tells a scientist more than the files say. RS-BULK-VIEW-M2 labels it rRNA genes and not rRNA contamination.

The globin cell of the samples table of `rnaseq quality` reads Not recorded for every result, and its facts say that no rule names the globin genes yet. A person who looks for the globin share of a blood sample gets none (C5 holds 14% to 22% globin by the human symbols, SEQC `A_1` 0.17%). A rule by symbol would read falsely low on the macaque sets and print a small share with no word that the main globin genes were missing, which is an S1 if it ships. The rule for the follow-up: the globin gene ids of a set are listed in the set when it is built, chosen by a person from the set's own gene table and the annotation's product text, with the list's sha256 in the record. The share then reads no globin genes listed when the set lists none, and Not recorded for a result with no reference set (every import).

A person who imports a single-cell result from the Import Center card never sees the words a script user sees, such as `so check the BAM's tags and barcodes` and `cells not computed (no ambient pool or no rRNA mask)`. With `--format json` the summary line of the command goes to stderr and `CLIImportRunner` keeps stderr only for a failure, so the Operations row reads only `Imported <name>.lungfishrnaseq`. The per-sample words are in the record. BIO rates it. A fix is a warning-level event from the command.

The unit row of the bulk RNA-seq import sheet reads `A count table states no unit, so choose what its numbers count. salmon's own numbers are estimated counts.` and nothing says that a table of TPM or other normalized values is not a count table, so a person can record TPM as Estimated counts. BIO rates it.

The two RNA-seq import sheets are fixed at 580 x 440 and 580 x 560 points with no scroll view, and each sample adds a BAM row of about 34 points once a reference set is chosen. By the review's count of text lines about five samples plus the outside note and a refusal need more than 560 points, so Import and Cancel can leave the panel (Return and Escape still act). Not rendered yet: walk row W-3 reads it with a set of many folders.

Refusal words of `import rnaseq` that name a flag the sheet does not show reach the sheet as the command wrote them, so a person reads `--genome`, `--samples`, `--not-host-bam`, `--unit` or `--tx2gene` where the field has another name (`Name every genome of the reference with --genome, or none.` against the field Genomes). A map from flag to field name would close it. The way back that RS-GLUE-UX SF-3 adds softens it.

A failed import row reads `CLI exited with status N` or `lungfish-cli binary not found` (`CLIImportRunner.failure(for:)`), which says what happened and not what to try. The runner is shared by every import, the RNA-seq cards included.

The Masks row of `docs/contracts/CLI-EQUIVALENCE.md:45` has no sentence for the `createdAt` of `rnaseq-result.json` (a wall-clock time, which the first words of the row cover) or for the checksum and size of its `sourceFiles` entries, and `MaskPolicy.standard` reads that file as payload text (its name holds neither `manifest` nor `provenance`, and `sizeKeys` has no `size`), so it hides none of them. Two parity cases hide them with test-local policies, `.rnaSeqImport` (`FastqIngestCancelReplayTests.swift`) and `.rnaSeqQuant` (`RNASeqQuantParityMasks.swift`), though the row says a mask is added only by a reviewed change. A later parity case of the family that copies neither fails on a race of one second. ARCH decides whether the family gets a reviewed row. If it does, the masks move into `standard` and the two policies go.

While Quantify RNA-seq Reads runs, its row in the Operations panel shows no progress and no step, only the lines the command writes to standard error, because `lungfish-cli rnaseq quant` prints no `CLIEvent` lines. A person who quantifies several samples sees no sign of how far salmon has come until the row ends or fails. A progress event from the command, one per sample, would fill the row.

At the command line, a fold-change bar that starts with a minus sign, as in `rnaseq export --lfc-bar -1`, is read by the argument parser as a missing value. The person reads `Error: Missing value for '--lfc-bar <lfc-bar>'`, a Help line and two Usage lines (exit 64, run on the built command), and not the sentence of the command's own check, `--lfc-bar is a log2 fold change of 0 or more, such as 1.` That sentence is reached only when the value is joined with an equals sign, as in `--lfc-bar=-1`, which the same build printed. The cutoff has the same gap, since `--padj-cutoff -0.05` printed `Error: Missing value for '--padj-cutoff <padj-cutoff>'` and not its own sentence. A candidate fix, not tried, is the parser's `.unconditional` parsing strategy on both options, so that a value that starts with a dash reaches `validate()`. At error rate 0.15 those reads land at about the chance rate of a read with no barcode in reach, which the chance floor measures (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Demultiplex/DemultiplexChanceFloor+Run.swift:254`). The Preview that carries the fix above 0/0 carries this notes line, and so do the known-issue lines of the page of Stable 2026.11.7 (`docs/contracts/SCOPE-AND-DELIVERY.md:23`). If your barcodes sit in from the read ends, set each distance to the farthest they sit in." and UX checks its words.

A run at 3' End with one moved read, one with Set B, one with a sample sheet that stays out of the check and one with an interleaved pair would close it. No result is wrong today.

Cutadapt cuts each read's final G bases before it searches, since the run passes `--nextseq-trim=20` for the Illumina kits (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Demultiplex/DemultiplexingPipeline.swift:2057-2060`, `Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Demultiplex/DemultiplexConfig.swift:240`, `Sources/LungfishIO/Formats/FASTQ/SequencingPlatform.swift:73`), and the check reads the read as cut (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Demultiplex/DemultiplexingPipeline+OffsetShift.swift:187` and `:670-672`, read at f4f39b411). A read whose 3' index sits at the read end and ends in G loses that base as a deletion. At error rate 0 no anchored line fits and the read goes to Unassigned, and at 0.15 an 8-base index tolerates one G, so only GG, or G and one more error, is lost. On made sets with each row's molecule at the read ends, both strands, the pipeline put 48 of 192 TruSeq HT Dual reads in Unassigned at error rate 0 and 12 at 0.15 (the D503 rows), and 52 of 168 Nextera XT v2 reads at 0 and none at 0.15 (`Tests/LungfishWorkflowTests/DemultiplexLinkedOffsetShiftTests.swift:294-333` at 0841af8ee). 3' End single-index runs meet it too, since TruSeq Single A D701, D709 and D712 and Set B D505 end in G, and a Custom Definition's barcodes may. 5' End lines are not cut. No number is false and no read lands in another sample, because Unassigned holds the reads as cut, so the row is S3, and S2 on a real library with the 3' index flush at the read end, where a sample shows no reads with no word about the trim. The fix needs a design choice, since the trim also helps when a poly-G tail follows the index. It can search the 3' index on the untrimmed read and trim after, or protect the index from the cut. The test replaces the pins 48, 12, 52 and 0 with 0 at both rates, adds a 3' End TruSeq Single A D701 run and a poly-G tail case that still assigns, and asserts that Unassigned equals the input.
